pv.src: Wikidata Q2970684 (Chateau de Septfontaines / Schlass Siwebueren), 49°37'32"N 6°6'18"E; the Hotel-Restaurant Sieweburen sits on the same Rue des Septfontaines directly beside the chateau. Chateau anchor, restaurant within ~150m on same street. No venue-precise pin obtainable via WebSearch.

places.ad: 400 Rue des Sept Arpents, 1149 Luxembourg, Luxembourg
places.w: A former 1873 hunting lodge in the heart of the Bambësch forest, reached on a woodland walk, serving revisited Luxembourgish cooking — Judd mat Gaardebounen with bacon apples, vol-au-vent, game in season — with a donkey pasture next door for the kids. A local favourite listed by ELLE and Paperjam.

pv.src: Waze place pin (Juegdschlass restaurant-cafe, 400 Rue des Sept Arpents); cross-checked to Beggen/Dommeldange corridor

places.w: The convivial brewery brasserie inside the Brasserie Nationale in Bascharage, where Bofferding and Battin are brewed — wooden tables, malt in the air, French-Luxembourgish plates and, of course, the freshest possible beer. Recommended by ELLE and Visit Luxembourg.

pv.src: en.wikipedia Bascharage (town); Avenue du Luxembourg 148

places.w: A confectionery-pâtisserie institution since 1863, now in its sixth family generation and a Fournisseur de la Cour (royal warrant). Keeper of Luxembourg's sweet tradition — the autumn Quetschentaart — alongside chocolates, glaces and a fine-food counter in the Ville-Haute.

pv.src: Rue des Capucins street-level coordinate (Google Maps street pin); house #27 on this short Ville-Haute street

places.w: A pâtisserie-traiteur house on the Grand-Rue, a Fournisseur de la Cour celebrating Luxembourg gastronomy for over 60 years. Its signature is the Bamkuch — the soft, faintly caramelised Luxembourg 'tree cake' — beside fine pastries and savoury delicacies.

pv.src: venue coordinate (Grand-Rue 16, Oberweis) via Waze/maps directory; cross-checked to Grand-Rue, Ville Haute

places.w: Luxembourg's only micro-brewery, in the 500-year-old former Mousel brewery at the Rives de Clausen — original steam engines and vats among the tables, unfiltered house beer, and traditional Luxembourgish plates (the grilled pork knuckle is the pick). A Bavarian-style brewpub for families by day and young revellers by night.

pv.src: Clausen district (Wikidata Q519726); 12 Rives de Clausen

places.w: An elegant, classical restaurant on the heights above Remich commanding a sweeping view over the Luxembourg Moselle — the place to pair refined cooking with the valley's own Riesling, Pinot Gris and Crémant de Luxembourg. A MICHELIN-Guide address in the heart of the wine country.

pv.src: en.wikipedia Remich (town); Route de l'Europe 36

places.w: Sarreguemines' MICHELIN-starred table, a champion of tradition where the chef works with local market gardeners and buys whole animals to cure his own charcuterie. Classic, produce-driven cooking a stone's throw from the German border — the faience town's fine-dining benchmark.

pv.src: venue coordinate (Auberge Saint-Walfrid, Sarreguemines) via aggregator POI

places.ad: Marché Couvert, Place de la Cathédrale, 57000 Metz, France
places.w: A Metz institution inside the historic covered market — Mauricette's stall of Grand Est produce (cheeses, Vosges smoked charcuterie, made-to-measure boards) plus the 'L'assiette du Marché' where you sit down to quiche lorraine, tourte, potée and flammekueche. No visit to the market is complete without a stop here.

pv.src: Wikidata Q17073035 (Marche Couvert de Metz); stall inside the covered market

places.w: A MICHELIN-starred gourmet restaurant with boutique hotel and working winery in the wine village of Olewig, ringed by vineyards. Chef-vintner Wolfgang Becker pairs precise, creative cooking with Riesling from the family's own slate slopes — Trier's benchmark fine table (a simpler Becker's Weinhaus sits alongside).

pv.src: Trier (Hauptmarkt, Wikidata Q897212); Olewiger Strasse 206, Trier-Olewig, town-level

places.w: A traditional Trier restaurant on the Hauptmarkt, unique for its Roman menu cooked from the ancient cookbook 'De re coquinaria' of Apicius — Lucanian sausages, wine rolls, lamb in fig sauce — served alongside regional dishes in a Roman wine cellar. Recently relaunched under new stewardship.

pv.src: Wikidata Q897212 (Hauptmarkt Trier); at Hauptmarkt 5

places.w: A tiny, top-heavy half-timbered wine tavern of 1416 on Bernkastel's market square, pouring more than 50 Rieslings and reds from its own cultivation. One of the Middle Mosel's most characterful spots for a glass of cool slate-slope Riesling.

pv.src: en.wikipedia Bernkastel-Kues; historic Marktplatz/old town (Spitzhaeuschen)

places.w: A cosy, long-popular Trier restaurant in the pedestrian zone built around the potato in every form — homemade potato bread and soups, baked potatoes, dumplings — plus regional plates like Trierer Rahmfleisch and filled potato dumplings. Generous, good-value 'Omas Küche' in the heart of the old town.

pv.src: Trier Hauptmarkt (Wikidata Q897212); Fahrstrasse 13-14, town-level

places.ad: 17 Route de Luxembourg, L-5752 Frisange, Luxembourg
places.w: The former Léa Linster, now run by her son Louis, who took the family table to two MICHELIN stars in 2025 and was Gault&Millau Luxembourg 'Restaurant of the Year 2024'. Classic finesse reworked into minimalist, delicately spiced contemporary plates. One of only two two-star tables in the Grand Duchy.

pv.src: venue coordinate (Route de Luxembourg/Letzebuergerstrooss 17, Frisange) via Waze/maps; cross-checked to Frisange

places.ad: 9 Place de Clairefontaine, L-1341 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
places.w: A MICHELIN-starred institution behind a majestic façade in the heart of the Ville Haute, on the quiet Place de Clairefontaine. Chef Arnaud Magnier is a past-master of polished Gallic fare built on top produce — Bresse poultry, Dieppe scallops.

pv.src: venue GPS (Restaurant Clairefontaine, 9 Place de Clairefontaine) via maps/outdooractive listing

places.ad: 1 Rue de Remich, L-5331 Moutfort, Luxembourg
places.w: Cyril Molard's snug two-MICHELIN-star table in Moutfort, for years the only two-star in the country. Outstanding produce, subtle tangy acidity and classically leaning sauces that keep the spotlight on the main ingredient.

pv.src: venue coordinate (Ma Langue Sourit, Moutfort) via aggregator POI

places.ad: Hôtel Le Place d'Armes, Place d'Armes, L-1136 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
places.w: The MICHELIN-starred dining room of boutique hotel Le Place d'Armes, wrapped in gold leaf and Art Nouveau stained glass. Chef Fabrice Salvador — trained at Troisgros, Guérard and Darroze — cooks seasonal, organic-leaning French cuisine with Bresse poultry and small-boat fish.

pv.src: Place d'Armes square coordinate (Wikidata Q1414793); venue is inside Hotel Le Place d'Armes at #18 on this square

places.ad: Villa Pétrusse, Luxembourg City (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
places.w: Inside the restored 1880 Villa Pétrusse, Le Lys won a MICHELIN star less than a year after opening. Luxembourg native Kim De Dood — two stars at Saint-Pierre in Singapore — blends traditional Luxembourgish cuisine with big-boned Asian intensity.

pv.src: Avenue Marie-Thérèse area coordinate (geocode.xyz); venue is Villa Pétrusse, 1 Avenue Marie-Thérèse L-2132 (street-level)

places.w: Luxembourg's first Japanese restaurant, founded 1988 in the Grund and long in the MICHELIN Guide. Reinvented as 'Aké by Kamakura' with izakaya-style sharing menus, chef Akira Yasuoka works premium product into timeless recipes with no concession to Western tastes.

pv.src: geocode.xyz address geocode (4 Rue Munster, Grund); cross-checked to Grund/Alzette

places.ad: 46 Place Guillaume II, L-1648 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
places.w: A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand on central Place Guillaume II, cool and chic, built around Mediterranean and Middle-Eastern mezze — an array of up to 15 appetisers, dips and pâtés for sharing. The most accessible credentialled table in the city.

pv.src: Place Guillaume II square coordinate (Wikidata Q359872); venue #46 on this square (latitude.to satellite value was wrong and discarded)

places.ad: Rue Théodore Flammang, L-5618 Mondorf-les-Bains, Luxembourg
places.w: The gastronomic table of Casino 2000 in the spa town of Mondorf-les-Bains, where Breton chef François Jagut — Gault&Millau Luxembourg 'Chef of the Year 2025' — serves inventive, fresh French cuisine with award-winning sommelier Thierry Corona on wine.

pv.src: Casino 2000 building coordinate (Google Maps cid / virtualglobetrotting), value flagged approximate; restaurant Les Roses is inside the casino (5 Rue Flammang)

places.w: A MICHELIN-starred restaurant with rooms in historic Clausen, five minutes from the centre. Gourmet dining under a veranda or on a terrace overlooking the garden's vines and a water feature, run by Annabelle Hazard and Pascal Soutiran.

pv.src: Place Sainte-Cunégonde coordinate (geocode.xyz, #21 on square); venue at 2 Place Sainte-Cunégonde, Clausen

places.n: La Villa de Camille et Julien
places.w: A one-MICHELIN-star table in leafy Belair. Chef Julien Lucas — trained alongside Robuchon, Loiseau and Ducasse — builds precise plates on high-quality Gallic ingredients like Brittany lobster and Provence asparagus.

pv.src: official site lavilla.lu 'getting here' page — venue is now 5 Rue de Pulvermuehl L-2356 (Pulvermühl), NOT Belair; worklist address is stale

places.w: A contemporary gastronomic table in Strassen rated three toques by Gault&Millau, with chef Baptiste Heugens turning out refined, modern cooking. Among the higher-scoring kitchens in the Grand Duchy.

pv.src: venue coordinate — TWO6TWO is inside the Smets store, 262 Route d'Arlon (Smets store-locator/yellow directory); TripAdvisor flags 'temporarily closed'

places.w: An unpretentious yet trendy French bistro in Clausen (14/20 Gault&Millau), with a menu built for sharing, a bar of more than 50 gins and a lovely back terrace in fine weather.

pv.src: Montée de Clausen OSM coordinate (geoview.info), immediately adjacent to Plateau Altmünster #6; geoportail address page for #6 exists

places.ad: Place d'Armes, L-1136 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
places.w: A brasserie on the Place d'Armes serving typical Luxembourgish dishes — Judd mat Gaardebounen among them — alongside wood-fired pizza and coffee specialities, at fair prices in the heart of the old town.

pv.src: Place d'Armes square coordinate (Wikidata Q1414793); Brasserie/Cercle Cité fronts this square

places.ad: 6 Rue du Fort Niedergrünewald, L-2226 Luxembourg (Kirchberg), Luxembourg
places.w: An authentic trattoria in the Kirchberg business district (at the Sofitel Europe), where chef Rodolfo Serritelli's signature tagliatelle alla grana is finished tableside in a wheel of Parmesan.

pv.src: address coordinate for 6 Rue du Fort Niedergruenewald = Sofitel Luxembourg Europe (Radici is the Sofitel's restaurant), Kirchberg

places.ad: 101 Rue Adolphe Fischer, L-1521 Luxembourg (Gare), Luxembourg
places.w: A cosy specialty coffee shop in the Gare quarter pulling shots from Berlin master-roaster The Barn, with a case of kanelbullar, pistachio buns and vegan cakes. A fixture of Luxembourg's third-wave scene.

pv.src: maps.me cafe pin (Bloom, 101 Rue Adolphe Fischer, Place de la Gare); cross-checked to Gare district

places.w: A charming natural-wine bar in the Grund run by Rossi Petkova and Franz Dickes, pouring from some 730 organic and biodynamic wines across 18 countries — including the Luxembourg Moselle — with seasonal French plates, cheese and charcuterie.

pv.src: Rue Münster, Grund — bracketed by adjacent sourced house pins (Mosconi #13 = 49.608972,6.135806; Aké #4 = 49.60895,6.136); venue is 18 Rue Münster

places.w: Long held up as the best of Luxembourg's many Portuguese restaurants, a five-minute walk from the station in Bonnevoie. Extensive fish and seafood, with an outstanding trio de bacalhau. Luxembourg's large Portuguese community shows on the plate.

pv.src: venue coordinate (90 Dernier Sol, Bonnevoie) via findlatitudeandlongitude/maps; cross-checked to south Bonnevoie

places.w: A specialist in the cooking of Madeira — deep-fried black scabbard fish with banana and passion-fruit sauce, espetada on a bay-leaf skewer, bolo do caco — beautifully presented, a favourite of the city's Portuguese and Madeiran diaspora.

pv.src: venue is 2-4 Rue du Pont, Pfaffenthal; coordinate is the Pfaffenthal panoramic elevator at 2 Rue du Pont (adjacent landmark, same address block). NB: actual district is Pfaffenthal, not Ville Haute

places.w: A family-run artisan chocolate maker turning out very high-quality handcrafted pralines and bars — a stop on Luxembourg's small but serious chocolate map.

pv.src: Chocolaterie Genaveh, 1 Rue Philippe II, L-2340 (Ville Haute); Rue Philippe-II street coordinate (Wikidata Q61123310), venue #1

places.ad: Rue du Marché-aux-Herbes, L-1728 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
places.w: A much-loved café in a 15th-century building directly opposite the Grand Ducal Palace. The signature is the chocolate spoon — pick a flavour from the display, dip it in a jug of hot milk — plus generous brunches. A homegrown Luxembourg brand that has since expanded.

pv.src: Rue du Marché-aux-Herbes / Krautmaart street coordinate; venue is #20, directly opposite the Grand Ducal Palace

places.w: A tiny, wildly popular ramen bar near the station — reservations advised, especially at lunch — turning out proper tonkotsu and shoyu bowls. A high point of Luxembourg's growing Japanese-street-food scene.

pv.src: Rue Sainte-Zithe street coordinate (Google Maps /@ pin, 49.604735,6.127877); venue is 29 Rue Sainte-Zithe

places.ad: Place de Paris, L-2314 Luxembourg (Gare), Luxembourg
places.w: A ramen specialist on Place de Paris where you build a bowl from miso, tonkotsu or shoyu broths with fresh noodles and toppings — part of the Gare quarter's cluster of good Japanese kitchens.

pv.src: Rue du Fort Elisabeth street coordinate (Gare, off Place de Paris); venue is Kaito ramen, 29 Rue du Fort Elisabeth

places.w: From the Black Sheep group, a short, well-balanced burger menu built on free-range beef and homemade bread, with everything from classic fries to sweet-potato fries — a repeat pick in the city's burger round-ups.

pv.src: venue is 12 Rue Chimay, L-1333 Ville-Haute (geoportail #12 confirmed); point bracketed by adjacent sourced anchors Place d'Armes (49.6114,6.1290) and Rue Philippe II (49.6111,6.1281)

places.w: A warm, family Lebanese kitchen in Limpertsberg — 'Good & Honest Food' — built for sharing plenty of small mezze plates: perfect falafel, hummus, halloumi, couscous. No alcohol served but BYOB with no corkage, at very fair prices.

pv.src: venue is 66 Avenue Pasteur, Limpertsberg; geocode.xyz #64 Avenue Pasteur = 49.62038,6.11935 (adjacent house to #66)

places.ad: 2 Place Léon XIII, L-1929 Luxembourg (Bonnevoie), Luxembourg
places.w: A hidden treasure in Bonnevoie a stone's throw from the central station, widely credited with the best bò bún in Luxembourg — plus scented pho and crispy egg rolls.

pv.src: venue coordinate (2 Place Léon XIII, Bonnevoie) via maps/tripexpress; cross-checked to Bonnevoie (Place Léon XIII)

places.w: A Gault&Millau-listed seasonal gastronomic stop in refined surroundings beside the castle at Clervaux, gateway to the Family of Man exhibition and the northern Ösling.

pv.src: Wikidata Q5131949 (Clervaux Castle), 50°3'15.876"N 6°1'48.324"E. The restaurant is housed within the castle, so the castle coordinate places it within the venue complex (med, not house-precise).

places.ad: 11 Place du Théâtre, L-2613 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
places.w: A specialty café on Place du Théâtre in the Ville Haute pouring beans from French roaster Mokxa — filter coffee and brunch bowls, a fixture of Luxembourg City's third-wave scene.

pv.src: Wikidata Q15925751 (Place du Theatre, Ville Haute), 49°36'46.4"N 6°7'51.2"E. Venue is at 11 Place du Theatre, i.e. on this small square, so the square centroid places it within ~50m (med).

places.w: An institutional table on the Place de Chambre below the cathedral, where Maître Restaurateur Alexis Baudin cooks a local, seasonal and creative gastronomy through four blind menus (including a vegetarian one). A Gault&Millau toque and one of Metz's most reliable bench-mark kitchens.

pv.src: resto.fr/tripsaide venue POI (31 Place de Chambre, Metz)

places.w: A refined Italian table in the Outre-Seille quarter, ten minutes from the Centre Pompidou, listed by Gault&Millau and the MICHELIN Guide and holding the Maître Restaurateur title. Carefully sourced Italian and Provençal product — charcuterie, burrata, wild fish, pure-bred meats — around house pasta.

pv.src: aroundus.com venue page 'Le 83' (Outre-Seille, Metz; 83 rue Mazelle) - coordinate stated in result text

places.ad: 4 Place de la Comédie, 57000 Metz, France
places.w: Set in the former Saint-Marcel military pavilion of 1752 facing the opera-theatre, El Theatris serves inventive market bistronomie with wines by the glass and a large terrace on the pale cobbles of the Place de la Comédie. A Gault&Millau-listed city fixture.

pv.src: aleou/resto.fr venue POI (El Theatris, Place de la Comédie, Metz)

places.w: A traditional Lebanese table in a quiet lane at the foot of the cathedral, serving delicate mezze — creamy houmous, crisp falafel, fresh taboulé — that anchor Metz's lively Levantine dining scene.

pv.src: firmania/rankeat venue POI (11 Place de Chambre, Metz)

places.w: By the Saint-Epvre basilica in the old town, the house of Jean-François Adam (a Lorraine pâtisserie since 1883) keeps the trademarked Saint-Epvre cake — two almond-meringue discs, vanilla buttercream and crushed nougatine, registered since 1907 — alongside macarons de Nancy and bergamot sweets. Bearer of the 'Nancy Passions Sucrées' label.

pv.src: Anchor: Basilique/Place Saint-Epvre Nancy (fr.wikipedia 48d41'45"N 6d10'48"E); venue at 3 Place Saint-Epvre on the square

places.w: A three-MICHELIN-star destination hidden in a village near Wittlich on the edge of the Mosel/Eifel, long the life's work of Helmut Thieltges and now carried on at the top by Clemens Rambichler. Uncompromising, produce-driven classic French cuisine ranked among Germany's very best tables — a pilgrimage worth the detour off the river.

pv.src: WorldPlaces venue page (germany.worldplaces.me/places-in-dreis/3770566-waldhotel-sonnora) - OSM-derived venue coordinate stated in page text

places.w: A family estate in Trier's Olewig wine district (about 3 km from the centre), listed by the Deutsches Weininstitut, known for high-quality Riesling and Burgundy wines. Its cosy Weinstube pairs those wines with classic vintner's cooking — the authentic way to taste Trier as a wine town.

pv.src: Mapcarta OSM node (way W549313820, 'Weingut Deutschherrenhof', Trier-Olewig) - coordinate read from mapcarta page

places.w: In the vaulted cellars of the medieval Cusanusstift, the largest Riesling vinotheque on the Mosel — more than 150 wines from Mosel, Saar and Ruwer available by the glass, chosen each year by a jury. Rick Steves names it the place to start tasting Mosel wine; the single best one-stop introduction to the region's Riesling.

pv.src: Wikipedia 'St. Nikolaus-Hospital / Cusanusstift' (the venue building at Cusanusstraße 2) - published WGS84 coordinate

places.w: A family-run restaurant-cum-wine-tavern in a former butcher's shop, its walls crammed with antique wine tools and a little museum's worth of Mosel memorabilia. Hearty, seasonal Mosel-Franconian cooking — Pfännchen, grilled steaks, small plates to drink wine with — a beloved Traben-Trarbach institution since 1970.

pv.src: aroundus.com venue entry (Alte Zunftscheune, Neue Rathausstraße 15, Traben-Trarbach)

places.w: A Weinstube in the old town of Saarburg pouring 30-plus open wines and sekt from the family's own Saar vineyards alongside regional cooking. On the Saar edge of the Mosel wine country, where the cuisine takes as much from nearby France as from Germany.

pv.src: Mapcarta OSM node (way W194174992, 'Saarburger Hof' hotel, Saarburg) - coordinate read from mapcarta page

places.w: A family-run 4-star hotel on the road out to the Olewig vineyards whose Kraft Bräu, founded 1998, was the first house brewery in Trier — a beer pub and large beer garden alongside an upscale a la carte restaurant. Fresh, largely regional and organic cooking paired with award-winning craft beers, the local answer to the city's wine.

pv.src: Google Maps place pin !3d49.743367!4d6.6598923 for 'Hotel Restaurant Hausbrauerei Blesius Garten, Olewiger Str. 135, 54295 Trier' surfaced in search results.

places.w: A VDP estate growing wine in Leiwen since 1624, with parcels in the Leiwener Laurentiuslay, Trittenheimer Apotheke and Piesporter Goldtröpfchen, some 85% Riesling. A serious address for dry Grosses Gewächs and fine noble-sweet Mosel Riesling on one of the river's grandest loops.

pv.src: Falstaff winery listing (falstaff.com/ld/w/weingut-grans-fassian) structured coordinates for Weingut Grans-Fassian, Römerstraße 28, Leiwen.

places.w: Saarbrücken's temple of haute cuisine, in a Wilhelminian villa with its own park; a MICHELIN-Guide fixture (long a three-star, currently two) where Klaus Erfort serves an uncompromising, produce-driven classic French menu. The Saarland's flagship fine-dining address.

pv.src: Saarbruecken St. Johann (St. Johanner Markt); Mainzer Strasse 95, town-level

places.n: Victor's Fine Dining by Christian Bau
places.w: Germany's benchmark table right where Germany, France and Luxembourg meet, at Victor's Residenz-Schloss Berg. Christian Bau has held three MICHELIN stars uninterrupted since 2005 for a French haute cuisine fused early and brilliantly with Japanese product; ranked among the world's top ten on La Liste.

pv.src: Wikidata Q2240241 (Schloss Berg, Nennig); restaurant is inside the castle

places.w: Saarbrücken's oldest inn, on the St. Johanner Markt, brewing its own beer and plating the city's most robust Saarland cooking — Gefillde, the Saarland-Teller, hearty pub classics. The definitive place to eat the region's home kitchen in the capital.

pv.src: Wikidata Q15848504 (St. Johanner Markt); Am Stiefel 2, adjacent

places.w: A younger address on Mainzer Straße giving Saarland cooking a modern turn — 'Saarland tapas', Lyoner, hearty classics reworked. A good hidden-gem counterpoint to the old brew-houses.

pv.src: Saarbruecken St. Johann (St. Johanner Markt); Mainzer Strasse 3, adjacent

places.w: Metz's MICHELIN-starred table (starred since 2006), set inside the 1559 provisions store of the city's citadel at Hôtel La Citadelle. Chef Christophe Dufossé cooks refined, modern Lorraine cuisine anchored in regional produce.

pv.src: restovisio.com venue POI (Le Magasin aux Vivres / Hôtel La Citadelle, 5 av. Ney, Metz)

places.w: A Parisian-style bistro in Metz's historic centre, 350 m from the cathedral, serving traditional French cooking with a Lorraine accent — quiche lorraine, home-style plates, regional wines by the pichet. Listed by the Inspire Metz tourist office and highly rated across platforms.

pv.src: restovisio/toutendroit venue POI (9 rue du Faisan, Metz)

places.w: Probably the best-known address in the capital for genuine Luxembourgish home cooking, going 50 years — the national dish Judd mat Gaardebounen, Gromperekichelcher, Kniddelen — in a warm, rustic room in the heart of the Ville Haute.

pv.src: maps.me-derived venue coordinate for 4-6 Côte d'Eich; grade capped at med because placement could not be independently cross-checked (possible northward offset along Côte d'Eich)

places.w: A MICHELIN-starred Italian jewel in the riverside Grund below the old town; chef Ilario Mosconi's Relais & Châteaux table (18/20 Gault&Millau) works imported Italian product into refined pasta and tasting menus overlooking the Alzette.

pv.src: en.wikipedia Mosconi (restaurant) infobox; 13 Rue Muenster, Grund

places.w: A pâtisserie-traiteur institution on Place Guillaume II since 1922, keeper of Luxembourgish sweet-and-savoury tradition — the autumn Quetschentaart and the Rieslingspaschtéit created here in 1928 — alongside a deep cheese and fine-food counter.

pv.src: en.wikipedia Place Guillaume II; at no.18 on the square

places.w: The visitor cellars of Luxembourg's biggest wine-and-crémant cooperative, on the Moselle bank at Grevenmacher and founded in 1921. Taste and buy the Grand Duchy's Riesling, Pinot and — above all — its sparkling Crémant de Luxembourg where the river marks the German border.

pv.src: en.wikipedia Grevenmacher (town); Rue des Caves 12

places.w: Trier's classic Weinstube, in the 250-year-old Palais Kesselstatt directly opposite the Liebfrauenkirche and cathedral, pouring Rieslings from the 650-year Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt estate's steep-slate Mosel/Saar/Ruwer sites alongside hearty regional cooking, self-serve at the counter. The signature Riesling-Weinstube experience of the Roman city.

pv.src: Trierer Dom (en.wikipedia); Liebfrauenstrasse 10, adjacent to the cathedral

places.w: A half-timbered Weinstube in Bernkastel-Kues's fairy-tale old town, named for the world-famous Bernkasteler Doctor vineyard on the slate slope above it. The place to drink Middle-Mosel Riesling — the Doctor is one of Germany's most storied sites — with Mosel trout and vintner's roast.

pv.src: en.wikipedia Bernkastel-Kues; Hebegasse 5, old town

places.w: A cult currywurst-and-gin bar off the St. Johanner Markt using meat from Bliesgau cattle raised nearby, with vegan sauces too. Named best currywurst in Germany by the Süddeutsche Zeitung and West Germany's most popular by Falstaff (2023) — a genuine Saarbrücken institution of the young-scene kind.

pv.src: Mapcarta Kaltenbachstraße street node (W67711898) - coordinate of the short street the venue (No. 4) sits on; not the exact house pin

places.n: Restaurant Quack in der Villa Weismüller
places.w: Creative crossover cooking in a listed Jugendstil villa with a garden terrace in Alt-Saarbrücken. A MICHELIN-Guide listing and 84 Falstaff points make it one of the city's most charming higher-end tables below the two-star bench.

pv.src: Wikidata Q99978065 (Villa Weismüller heritage building) coordinate 49°13'56.35"N 6°57'58.43"E; the restaurant occupies this exact villa.

places.w: Hearty Saarland home cooking and pub classics under the 120-year-old brick vaults of the neo-Gothic St. Johann town hall. A reliable, atmospheric address for Gefillde, Schwenker and regional beer in the very centre of the city.

places.w: The epitome of the Nauwieser scene — regional, seasonal cooking (around half vegetarian) with many organic and fair-trade ingredients, hidden in a linden-shaded courtyard. A daily-changing Mittagstisch by day; by evening one of the coziest wine spots in the quarter.

pv.src: Mapcarta OSM node (way W338070457, 'Kultur- und Werkhof Nauwieser 19') = the Nauwieserstraße 19 building the cafe occupies - coordinate read from mapcarta page

places.w: Authentic Neapolitan pizza on Mainzer Straße — a dough of just flour, water, little yeast and sea salt rested up to 72 hours and baked at nearly 500°C. A young local favourite for soft, airy pies both classic and creative.

pv.src: Google Maps place pin (!3d49.2318023!4d6.9995368) for Gotti Pizza, Mainzer Str. 8 — read from place-pin, not viewport.

places.w: Sternekoch Cliff Hämmerle serves classic French cooking with creative, vegetable-forward touches from the surrounding UNESCO Bliesgau biosphere, split between the fine 'Barrique' room and the more affordable 'Landgenuss'. One MICHELIN star, 16 points in Gault&Millau and 7 pans in GUSTO; at the Chef's Table the chef plates and explains each course himself.

pv.src: Venue geocode from das-oertliche.de / gastroguide.de for Hämmerle's Restaurant, Bliestalstr. 110a, Blieskastel-Webenheim.

places.w: A MICHELIN-starred French kitchen in a green setting in the heart of St. Ingbert, 15 minutes from Saarbrücken, led by head chef Florian Dauphin and Lorena Jil. Seasonal dishes rooted in French tradition, offered à la carte or as a menu, with six guestrooms above — one of the top addresses in the Saarpfalz.

pv.src: Venue GPS geocode (cityseeker/novacircle listing) for Die Alte Brauerei, Kaiserstraße 101, St. Ingbert; matches main-street location north of centre.

places.w: Dillingen's upscale French address in the Stadthalle, where chef Fabrice Bertrand pairs traditional French cooking with modern, molecular flourishes (a simpler bistro 'Chez Fabrice' sits alongside). Carried by Falstaff and the state's own Saarland-erleben tourism guide — an elegant, chef-driven table in a town otherwise short on fine dining.

pv.src: Berckheimstraße 1 = the Dillingen (Saar) station/Stadthalle complex; Wikipedia station coordinate 49°21'09"N 6°43'21"E. Restaurant is in this building, so within ~150 m.

places.w: A brewpub right on the Saar at the Merzig marina (opened 2000) pouring three house beers — light, dark and wheat, plus a seasonal brew — with home-baked beer bread and Saarland-French brewery cooking known well beyond the town. A big beer garden with a sandy beach and playground makes it a family destination; brewery tours run on request.

pv.src: Approx. coordinate from geocaching.com listing GC203EF 'Saarfürst-Brauerei Merzig' (49°26.550'N 6°38.210'E) at the Merzig marina; brewery is at Saarwiesenring 6 by the yacht harbour SW of centre — within a few hundred m.

places.w: A brewpub set in Neunkirchen's industrial monument beside the old blast furnace, serving the full Saarland canon — Hoorische, Gefillde, Dibbelabbes with apple sauce, Eierschmeer and the classic Lyonerpfanne — as a 'Saarländer Tapas' plate, plus house-brewed beers, Bliesgau rye bread and game from the house's own hunting grounds. A regional flag-bearer for Saarland home cooking.

places.w: An independent 'Erlebnisbrauerei' (adventure brewery) with a large brewhouse tavern, gallery and 400-seat beer garden near the Saarschleife, brewing wholesome organic beer and serving hearty, seasonal regional cooking — even with its own mustard mill. A popular stop for cyclists, hikers and families around Mettlach.
